summary.oneLiner: Daily synthetic test leads through every client site's quote form, confirmed all the way to the inbox or CRM, sold to the agency that maintains the sites.
summary.buyer: Small web and marketing agencies that maintain 20-100 small-business client sites on retainer. They, not the plumber, see the same broken-form failure across many sites, take the blame when leads stop, and need proof that their maintenance retainer is worth paying for.
summary.problem: A contact or quote form shows its success message, but a plugin update, SMTP change or CRM integration failure means the lead never arrives. Uptime monitors and analytics still report healthy, so the failure is silent until the client notices a dry pipeline weeks later.
summary.solution: One engine submits a tagged test lead through each client site's real form on a schedule and checks that it lands at the destination (inbox, CRM or webhook). When it does not arrive, the agency gets an alert naming the site and the broken step, and every month gets a per-client report proving the lead path worked.

price.rationale: Priced per monitored site so it scales with the agency's book and can be passed through on the client's maintenance invoice; well under the value of a single recovered lead.

summary.whyNow: WordPress plugin churn and the move to authenticated email sending mean form delivery breaks more often, while agencies are under pressure to justify retainers with visible proof of work.
summary.whyItWins: Uptime and browser-automation tools stop at 'the page loaded' or 'the form submitted'. This is the only level that confirms the lead reached the business, and it is sold to the aggregator who feels the pain on every client site.
summary.nextAction: Interview five agency owners who maintain 30+ client sites, then run a free 30-day pilot on one agency's sites and show them the first silent failure it catches.

pitch.callScript: Open: ask how many client sites they maintain and how they find out when a form stops delivering. Probe: last time a client complained about missing enquiries, how long it took to notice. Offer: free 30-day pilot on their sites with a daily delivery test and an end-of-month report. Close: book the pilot setup call.

objections.response: Uptime confirms the page loads; this confirms the lead arrives. They catch different failures.
The pilot is free, so you lose nothing if it finds nothing, and you get a report to show clients either way.

pitch.pricingCopy: $8 per monitored site per month. Daily end-to-end lead tests, instant alerts when a form stops delivering, and a monthly per-client proof report. No setup fee, cancel anytime.
